findings.title: Coalesce selection cells before rasterizing
findings.message: Selection replay now performs a separate FillBounds operation for every selected grapheme, instead of one glyph-region fill per intersected run. Selecting a long, unwrapped line therefore issues thousands of raster fills on every replay, including cells outside the clip. Checking every range against every cell also introduces O(cells × ranges) intersection work.
findings.suggestion: Coalesce adjacent selected cells with matching vertical bounds into rectangles before calling FillBounds, and reject rectangles outside the clip. Return immediately when ranges is empty; for many ranges, normalize them and use an indexed or sweeping intersection lookup.

findings.title: Merge cluster geometry before expanding to grapheme boundaries
findings.message: Rounding each shaping cluster outward independently can produce multiple cells for the same grapheme rather than one cell covering its complete advance. For example, clusters [0,1) and [1,2) with grapheme boundaries [0,2] both become cells for [0,2], each covering only its own advance. This can occur when a grapheme crosses font/style runs, and makes its caret endpoints and selection geometry ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate cluster advances belonging to the same grapheme before emitting cells. Handle graphemes spanning runs in the interaction-layout aggregation as well, and add a regression test with a base character and combining mark split across shaping clusters or styled runs.

finding.title: Clip selection and highlights to the text viewport
finding.message: Selection and highlight backgrounds are rendered before the text viewport clip is installed. Since autoScroll now exposes the entire paragraph rather than a visible substring, selecting or highlighting horizontally scrolled text can paint outside the text viewport, including over icon areas.
finding.suggestion: Push the text viewport context before rendering highlights and selection, so their backgrounds are clipped along with the text.
finding.evidence:
tf.renderHighlights()
	tf.renderSelect()
	pc := &tf.Scene.Painter
	pc.PushContext(nil, render.NewBoundsRect(tf.textViewport(), tf.Styles.Border.Radius.Dots()))

fix.before:
tf.renderHighlights()
	tf.renderSelect()
	pc := &tf.Scene.Painter
	pc.PushContext(nil, render.NewBoundsRect(tf.textViewport(), tf.Styles.Border.Radius.Dots()))
fix.after:
pc := &tf.Scene.Painter
	pc.PushContext(nil, render.NewBoundsRect(tf.textViewport(), tf.Styles.Border.Radius.Dots()))
	tf.renderHighlights()
	tf.renderSelect()
